g.title: ArthurRank6Convo4 begins.
g.text: ArthurRank6Convo4 begins.

g.title: j408319438
g.text: Odd question. Do they have toys in space?

g.title: j1263929547
g.text: Like, children's toys? Of course.

g.title: j1578366175
g.text: What... kind of toys?

g.title: j387694213
g.text: Heh. Really?

g.title: j525162145
g.text: OH, SOL. That's not what I meant, and you know it!

g.title: j3312790162
g.text: Hard to picture some umpteenth-some-odd-whatever thousands of years in the future,

g.title: j1596767414
g.text: I mean, children's toys. Dolls. Action figures. Things like that.

g.title: j3986594818
g.text: Kids are still sitting around reenacting stories with little figurines and playing "bandits" or "save the princess."

g.title: j1877919595
g.text: Just giving you a hard time. :P

g.title: j3341196529
g.text: No, we don't. [End.]

g.title: j3206087200
g.text: What brought this on?

g.title: j2715800952
g.text: What did you grow up playing with?

g.title: j2444560503
g.text: We have different names for the games we play, but I definitely had toys.

g.title: j4260157313
g.text: Yeah, of course we do.

g.title: Chat ends.
g.text: Chat ends.

g.title: j6193351
g.text: I was actually watching Amir playing one of his arcade games.

g.title: j484541311
g.text: It's rather comforting thinking that despite all the differences between our cultures, kids still just... sit down and play with toys.

g.title: j3473637151
g.text: Like what?

g.title: j931051472
g.text: And I was thinking to myself - what I wouldn't give to have that kind of joy in my life again.

g.title: j3124688529
g.text: I had this action figure. Action Angus. He was a soldier, no surprise there.

g.title: j518221768
g.text: All sorts of figurines, and stuffed animals, and blocks. Typical kid stuff.

g.title: j18304627
g.text: I had this one - I guess you could call it a figurine - of this Dax child, that, well, I named after a character in a book I had. Dominus Thrax.

g.title: j566342218
g.text: I've never looked down my nose at Aoi, or Amir, or even now Kaya for finding fun in "childish" things. It's never bothered me.

g.title: j1407560912
g.text: One solstice celebration, a bunch of the older boys stole it from me along with a bunch of my other toys and, well...

g.title: j555612916
g.text: Oh, bollocks. I should've known. I'm so sorry that I brought this up.

g.title: j2407314059
g.text: But sometimes I'm afraid that the part of me that's capable of feeling that curled up and died a long time ago.

g.title: j719236302
g.text: It's a long story. Short of it? I was "too old," they said, to be playing with dollies. That was the last time I ever played with toys.

g.title: j1367780169
g.text: Not the best topic for me to discuss, no.

g.title: j3513696562
g.text: It's all right. It's not your fault.

g.title: j3629987731
g.text: Kind of sad, isn't it? That we tell children to love something, and then we tell them to give it up when they've "matured."

g.title: j2055951009
g.text: The other day, I was watching Amir play one of his games. It's clear how much he's attached it. How much happiness it brings him. And I was a bit jealous that I don't have anything like that in my life.

g.title: j2979701950
g.text: Now I feel like an absolute knobhead.

g.title: j1221557722
g.text: We had all the normal toys you'd expect, I suppose. Blocks, stuffed animals, figurines, dolls.

g.title: j4282288749
g.text: I don't know. We all have to grow up sometime. We can't hide ourselves away with make-believe. I learned that the hard way.

g.title: j618415722
g.text: I think life can be ugly and painful and short. And we should fill it with as much fun, and laughter, and love as we can find.

g.title: j429771563
g.text: Mine only became a little more problematic because of the whole... Void thing.

g.title: j3624449156
g.text: You make a fair point. I think when it becomes a replacement for the real thing, it's a problem. I'm not suggesting that.

g.title: j1205297577
g.text: You're right. And I hope it's something we remember, as we go forward together in... whatever this is that we're in.

g.title: j2546049378
g.text: You know, I found Eleanor, Velimir, Aoi, and Amir, playing hide-and-seek with Flare and Lizzie. (Quincy said he wasn't allowed to play because the bastard was cheating and was using his scope to see through walls.)

g.title: j3697925924
g.text: They were all looking at me worried I was going to be upset I caught them mucking about when they should be doing something useful.

g.title: j4237189351
g.text: I was more upset that I wasn't invited. Heh. But I had to put on the grumpy leader face and pretend I was upset that the posts were left unmanned, etcetera.

g.title: j1019511816
g.text: But Amir has his games. Aoi has On-lyne. Even Kaya has her stickers and her Jinymon, for all that the world has forced adulthood on her too soon.

g.title: j1122412657
g.text: Is there a point you're trying to make?

g.title: j553041465
g.text: I think it's something you could get back, if you tried. Finding joy in toys and games, I mean.

g.title: j4146223720
g.text: Honestly? I'm not even sure. Only that I feel like I'm missing something that's been gone from my life for a very long time.

g.title: j885688958
g.text: I can just hear the laughter now. But I suppose that's really what's holding me back, isn't it? Embarrassment.

g.title: j2856420394
g.text: I'm not sure if I can ever get it back. Or if it's too far gone. But who knows. With enough time, maybe anything is possible.

g.title: j3546357931
g.text: I'm not sure it's possible to get it back, even if I could push through the momentary shame. But who knows. With enough loops, maybe anything is possible.
